issues.description: The problem statement requires the function 'start_app' to be the global entry point, but the template defines and exports 'main' (global main) and does not provide 'start_app'. The solution defines a 'start_app' label but does not declare it global (comment even notes the mismatch). This inconsistency about which symbol should be global will confuse students and can prevent the program from being used as the specified entry point (and may break automated checks expecting a global 'start_app').
issues.suggestedFix: Make the entry-point requirement consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the template to export 'start_app' (replace 'global main' with 'global start_app' and provide a start_app label that calls the existing main logic), and update the solution to declare 'global start_app' as well; or (B) change the problem statement to require 'main' as the global entry point. The preferred fix is to export 'start_app' in both template and solution so they match the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement requires the program entry point to be the function named 'start_app', but the template defines and exports 'main' as the global entry symbol. The solution file contains a 'start_app' label that is not exported as global while 'main' remains global. This inconsistent naming of the same conceptual entity (the program entry point) across problem, template, and solution will confuse students about which symbol they must provide/export.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the entry-point identifier across all artifacts. Preferably update the template and solution to export and use 'start_app' as the global entry point (replace 'global main' with 'global start_app' and ensure the executable code is under the 'start_app' label). Alternatively, change the problem statement to require 'main' if that is intended.
